evidence.quote:
whoever held his finger in the smoke of
      the kitchen-pot, immediately smelt all the dishes that were cooking on
      every hearth in the city
evidence.paraphrase: The kitchen-pot has a described capability: touching its smoke lets one smell all dishes cooking throughout the city.

evidence.quote:
he at last constructed a rattle, which, when it was
      swung round, played all the waltzes and jig tunes, which have ever been
      heard since the creation of the world
evidence.paraphrase: A constructed rattle is described as able to play every waltz and jig tune ever heard.

evidence.quote:
this, you see, was something quite
      different from the rose
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator directly contrasts the pot's function with the earlier natural rose gift for the reader.

evidence.quote: But the Princess touched it, and was almost ready to cry.
evidence.paraphrase: The Princess reacts with disappointment upon touching the rose.

evidence.quote: It is not made at all, it is natural!
evidence.paraphrase: The Princess expresses disdain because the gift is natural rather than manufactured.

evidence.quote:
the ladies of the court; I must
      go down and see what they are about!
evidence.paraphrase: The Emperor reacts with curiosity and rubs his eyes on seeing the crowd by the pigsty.

evidence.quote:
both Princess
      and swineherd were thrust out of the city
evidence.paraphrase: The Emperor's anger results in both the Princess and swineherd being expelled from the city.
